claims.assertion: The trip deviated well beyond tolerance: actual distance 9.6 km against an optimal 3.9 km, +5.7 km (+144%), so the RD-1 no-refund threshold of 1 km is far exceeded and the deviation must be priced under RD-2.
The metered fare billed $7.99 of excess distance (5.67 km × $1.4100/km), of which RD-2 refunds the excess distance fare and not the time fare, tolls or surge.

The first off-route segment (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km) was agreed: the driver asked at 14:01 "ok if I go round by Cavenagh?" and the rider answered at 14:02 "Sure", and Cavenagh Road is the first road the segment actually drove — so that 1.85 km is exempt under RD-3/RD-5, and because it was traffic-motivated and informed, no violation attaches to it.

The rider's only other request was the general "Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?" (14:02), which names no place or road, so it is at most a general route choice and cannot exempt the second segment's route.

The second off-route segment (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km) ran NICOLL HIGHWAY → MIDDLE ROAD → BEACH ROAD → REPUBLIC AVENUE → REPUBLIC BOULEVARD → RAFFLES AVENUE with no rider message agreeing to Beach Road; the rider's complaint says explicitly she asked only for a quick 7-Eleven stop, not a drive out to Beach Road.

The 4 min 10 s stop at 14:20–14:24 was 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off and not a pickup or drop-off point, and the driver's own statement places the 7-Eleven he chose on Beach Road — a place the rider never named and that was disclosed only after the trip, so it is the driver's chosen stop, not an agreed one.

No traffic justification covers the second segment: the recorded congestion is on Orchard Road (band 1, 14:00–14:10) and the accident at 13:52 was on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road on the optimal route the first segment avoided, while Bras Basah Road (band 4) and Bayfront Avenue (band 3) were free-flowing, so the Beach Road loop has no traffic reason under RD-4.

The driver gave no notice before or at the start of the second segment (the last message before it was his bare "Ok" at 14:03), so the Beach Road reroute is an uninformed deviation and takes a driver-violation record plus a notification-duty reminder.
Refundable distance = 5.67 − 1.85 = 3.82 km at $1.4100/km = $5.39, which is the excess distance fare for the unexempt segment and must be refunded as refund_partial.

The driver has 1 upheld dispute in the last 90 days and 812 trips, but because that upheld dispute is a no-show rather than a route deviation, RD-6's repeat-deviation flag is not triggered on this record; the profile is offered only as context.

weaknesses: The rider did answer "Sure" to the driver's 14:01 proposal in F9, and Cavenagh Road is inside the first segment's roads driven (F4), so 1.85 km is genuinely exempt and my refund is reduced by that amount.

The rider did ask for a "7-Eleven" stop (F10) and the driver did stop for 4 min 10 s (F2); the driver will argue that stop was the requested one, which is why the place question under RD-3:F5 turns on whether a 7-Eleven on Beach Road — never named by the rider (F13 is a post-trip statement) — can be the place she named.

The driver will argue RD-4 traffic justification using the band 1 Orchard Road congestion and the 13:52 accident (F14, F17), though those were on the avoided part of the optimal route and Bras Basah/Bayfront were free-flowing (F15, F16).
The time fare of $6.89 on a 26.5 min trip (F8, F3) is not recoverable on this dispute type, so the refund I request is only a fraction of the $25.81 charged (F8).

claims.assertion: Both off-route segments were driven on a route the rider agreed to before the trip: the driver asked at 14:01 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' and the rider answered at 14:02 'Sure.', a rider message sent before the first segment began at 14:10. Segment F4's roads driven include CAVENAGH ROAD, so the named road the rider agreed to is exactly the one driven.

The reroute had a traffic reason: an accident closed two lanes on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road at 13:52, 0 m from the optimal route and still before both segments, and ORCHARD ROAD was in speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) from 14:00 to 14:10, the recommended route's own corridor. The driver's stated reason ('Orchard was jammed after an accident') is therefore corroborated by the traffic record, not merely asserted.

The 14:17–14:29 segment (F5) was not the driver's errand: it exists to reach the stop the rider herself asked for at 14:02 ('Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?'), and the car stopped for 4 min 10 s at 14:20–14:24 at a point 2,995 m from pickup / 2,098 m from drop-off — not at the pickup or the drop-off, i.e. a mid-trip stop matching that request. That stop time is chargeable as time fare under RD-3, so the waiting line is $0.00 (F8).

The total deviation is +5.7 km (9.6 km actual vs 3.9 km optimal), of which 1.85 km (F4) and 2.87 km (F5) are the two billed segments — so even on the rider's reading the refundable item is the excess distance fare of $7.99, not the whole $25.81 charged; base $3.90, time $6.89 and platform $1.47 are unaffected by distance, and surge was 1.0× so no surge differential arises.

The rider's 'quick 7-Eleven' message named no place and no road, and the driver neither named Beach Road nor said he would deviate to it; the Beach Road portion of F5 was simply how the driver got from the agreed stop back to the destination. The complaint's framing that the rider 'only asked for a quick 7-Eleven stop' does not by itself show any named road in the record for the return leg.

The driver has one upheld route-related deviation in the last 90 days? No — his record shows 1 upheld dispute and it is a no-show, not a route deviation, so there is no basis to add flag_account for repeat route deviation, and his 4.0-year, 812-trip account with a 4.7 rating supports no aggravation of the outcome.

weaknesses: For F5, the rider's message (F10) names a shop type, not a place: 'a 7-Eleven on the way'. The rider will argue the driver chose the specific outlet himself (his statement, F13, says he stopped at 'the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road'), so RD-3's 'rider named a place' is arguably not satisfied for the segment that drove BEACH ROAD, and — because the rider named no road for that leg — RD-5's road-name check may come back 'escalate' (no road names in the record for the agreed route there).

The rider will press that F5 drove 2.87 km extra with a maximum 1,553 m excursion from the optimal route and that the stop sits 2,995 m from pickup (F2): that pattern can be read as an errand of the driver's own rather than a stop 'on the way', which would move F5 to driver_errand and expose a driver violation under RD-2/RD-3.

The consent in F10 ('Sure.') answers only the driver's Cavenagh proposal, which on the record covers the F4 corridor; the rider will argue it cannot also cover the later, separate leg that included BEACH ROAD (F5) and REPUBLIC AVENUE/BOULEVARD, roads never mentioned before the segment.

If the judge reads F5 as non-exempt despite the traffic reason, RD-4 does not exempt the segment from refund — it only decides whether a violation is recorded (RD-2) — so the excess distance fare of $7.99 (F6) stands as a refundable amount on the rider's side, and the only live argument left is whether a driver violation is recorded (the traffic record in F17/F14 is the driver's best answer to that).

points.response: I concede the Cavenagh part and only that: the rider's 14:02 "Sure." (F10) answers the driver's 14:01 ask "ok if I go round by Cavenagh?" (F9) and CAVENAGH ROAD is the first road of the 14:10–14:15 segment, so that segment's 1.85 km is exempt — but that yes reaches one named road for one segment, not the later 14:17–14:29 leg that drove BEACH ROAD and REPUBLIC AVENUE (F5), roads never mentioned before the segment.

The traffic reason is real and I do not contest it: the accident at 13:52 closed two lanes on Orchard Road after Cavenagh Road 0 m from the optimal route and ORCHARD ROAD sat in band 1 from 14:00 to 14:10 (F17, F14). Under RD-4 that reason decides only whether a violation is recorded for the Cavenagh segment; it does not exempt any segment from the distance refund on the Beach Road leg, where Bras Basah Road ran at band 4 and Bayfront Avenue at band 3 (F15, F16).

The stop itself is not in dispute, but the driver's own words supply the errand: he was asked for a 7-Eleven "on the way" (F10) and after the trip wrote that he stopped at "the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road" (F13) — a specific outlet he chose, 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off (F2), with the leg reaching 1553 m off the optimal route (F5), so the loop that got him there is the driver's own, not the rider's named place; under RD-3 an accepted stop is chargeable in time fare only, it does not licence 2.87 km of extra distance.

Agreed on quantum shaping only: the refundable item is the excess distance fare and not the $25.81 total, nor the $6.89 time fare or the $1.47 platform fee, and surge at 1.0× creates no differential (F7, F8). But the distance refund is computed after subtracting only the exempt km: 5.67 − 1.85 = 3.82 km × $1.4100 = $5.39 (F6, F1), not the full $7.99.

The absence of a named road is why this leg is not exempt: with no rider message before 14:17 agreeing to the roads of F5, the segment is consent_after_or_none under RD-5, and the driver's only message ahead of it was a bare "Ok" at 14:03 (F11) that says nothing about Beach Road; a 2.87 km, 1553 m excursion (F5) is not "how the driver got back to the destination" on a route whose optimal leg is 0.77 km.

I do not seek a repeat-deviation flag and my brief already says so: the driver's one upheld dispute is a no-show, not a route deviation, so RD-6 is not triggered (F20). I do ask that the uninformed Beach Road reroute be logged as a driver violation and that a notification-duty reminder issue, since the notice condition of RD-5 failed (F11, F5).

I raise my own number to meet the opponent's counsel: they themselves argue F5's 2.87 km is non-exempt, and on the record only the 1.85 km Cavenagh segment is covered, so the refundable distance is the whole 5.67 km of F6 minus the Cavenagh 1.85 km (F4) — 3.82 km × $1.4100 = $5.39; the $3.70 the driver offers corresponds to no arithmetic in F4, F5 or F6.

Conceded as far as it goes: +5.7 km (F1) exceeds the 1 km tolerance under RD-1, but the total deviation is not the refundable amount — RD-2 prices only the excess distance fare, and per F6 that excess is $7.99, not the $25.81 charged (F8).

Agreed on the arithmetic: $7.99 of the bill is excess distance (F6) and RD-2 refunds excess distance fare only, leaving base, time and platform components (F8) untouched; the dispute is only about which km are exempt under RD-3/RD-5.

No disagreement: F4's roads driven open with CAVENAGH ROAD and the rider's 14:02 'Sure.' (F10) answers the driver's 14:01 Cavenagh proposal (F9), so the 1.85 km of F4 is exempt as rider-agreed (RD-5) and, with the 13:52 accident 0 m from the optimal route and Orchard Road in band 1 from 14:00–14:10 (F17, F14), carries no violation. I take this concession as agreed between the advocates.

The recorded exchange is not read in halves: the rider's 14:02 message is a single sentence — 'Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' (F10) — which first accepts the Cavenagh route and then asks for a stop on that route, and the driver answered 'Ok' at 14:03 (F11) before the first segment began at 14:10 (F4); the stop request is therefore an agreed scope element of the same pre-trip agreement, not a stray remark, and RD-3 says stop time is chargeable as time fare — indeed waiting billed is $0.00 (F8).

F5's 2.87 km exists to reach and return from the stop the rider asked for at 14:02 (F10): the car halted 4 min 10 s at 14:20–14:24 at a point 2,995 m from pickup and 2,098 m from drop-off — neither the pickup nor the drop-off (F2) — so the Beach Road corridor is how the driver served her request, not a sightseeing detour; and her message named no road for that leg at all, so the RD-5 road-name check has nothing to test and no named road was overridden.

The placement of the outlet is the one point I cannot defend: F10 names only 'a 7-Eleven on the way' and F13, written after the trip, states the driver 'stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road', so the specific outlet was the driver's choice and RD-3's 'rider named the place' is not met for the segment that turned down BEACH ROAD (F5); that is exactly why my segment ground for F5 has moved to consent_after_or_none, and the rider's agreement to the stop limits recovery of the route beyond the stop itself.

The traffic record does support the reroute: F17 records the 13:52 accident 'on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road, two lanes closed' at 0 m from the optimal route, and that incident started before the 14:17 segment and remained active, which satisfies RD-4 on the recommended route; F14's band 1 (0–9 km/h) on ORCHARD ROAD during 14:00–14:10 confirms the corridor was still blocked when the driver committed to going round, and F15/F16 (bands 4 and 3 on Bras Basah and Bayfront) says nothing about the closed lanes on Orchard Road the driver avoided.

The notice duty was discharged before the first movement: the driver's 14:01 message gave the reason and the route 'traffic on Orchard is bad, ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' (F9) and the rider acknowledged at 14:02 (F10), which is notice 'before or at the point of deviation' under RD-5 for the agreed loop she asked to include a stop; the record shows a complete, timestamped 3-message exchange (F12), so there is no uninformed-reroute finding and no RD-7 reminder follows.

The subtraction is one-sided: it exempts the 1.85 km of F4 but charges the driver the full 2.87 km of F5 even though the rider's own request (F10) is what placed the car on that leg and the rider never named a road for it — on the record's plain reading the second segment too was driven to serve the agreed stop (F2), so the only defensible residual is the distance beyond what the rider's request reached, which on my reading is short enough to fall to a nominal amount, not $5.39.

Agreed: F20 shows the one upheld dispute in 90 days is a no-show, not a route deviation, so RD-6's repeat-deviation flag is not triggered and no flag_account should be added; F19 and F20 are context only and decide nothing (TH-3).
